final_verdict.summary: The footage matches the earliest copy found, published on 2021-07-03 (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=W0xvQCfDZOY, date independently fetched per yt-dlp metadata), before the claimed event date 2023-10-06. Matcher evidence: 16 temporally consistent frame(s), up to 97 inliers. This shows the footage was previously published; it does not by itself show the footage is fake or that the claimed event did not happen. Separately, the AI visual clues report 2 unverified observation(s) that clash with the claim (e.g. "Architecture, vertical Japanese signage and Japanese-type vehicles point to Japan, not Sikkim, India", frame ref [20, 27, 34]); these are model observations, not independent evidence and not part of the visual-match proof.
limits: A visual match proves shared footage ('previously published'), not that a claim is false or that the footage is fake.
Upload dates are platform metadata (or an archive snapshot date, an upper bound) for the copy found; the earliest copy found is not necessarily the original source.
Search is not exhaustive: memory covers only indexed clips, reverse search rarely finds originals, and heavy crops/edits can evade hash shortlisting.
'Not found' means not found by these adapters, not that no earlier copy exists.
